summary:
I read every changed source and test file at 7d80237 and ran the whole solution through eng/dotnet.ps1: it built, and 86 of 86 tests passed with none skipped. I walked all 13 case rows. Each named test builds the shape its row describes on real NTFS, including a folder whose only child is a subfolder three levels deep, and nothing I read builds an easier shape than it claims. O-001 to O-013 are all in the code where the builder says.

I measured two things myself:
- A 72 MiB LZNT-compressed file, which the new large-file probe now opens, gave the same size from the listing and from FILE_STANDARD_INFO (alloc 9,437,184). So that probe does not over-count on-disk size for compressed files.
- I deleted the `!cloudOnly &&` guard from SizeProbe.IsDue and all 86 tests still passed. The large-file probe's cloud guard is not held by any test: the only OFFLINE fixture is 1 MiB, so it reaches the WOF check only. I restored the file from HEAD and checked it matches.

Three minor findings, none blocking:
1. The untested cloud guard above.
2. MainWindow catches every ArgumentException subclass, so an internal ArgumentOutOfRangeException shows "Could not read" instead of "Scan failed".
3. The engine's Fitness gate reports no rules (there is no .taad/fitness.yaml). The architecture rules are enforced only by ArchitectureRulesTests.

The code matches the as-built design in docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md. Apart from finding 2, the departures from the original design were declared. The slice is not stuck in a loop: build attempt 2 was sent back by the critique and changed 11 src files.

findings.claim: Attempt 2 added a third probe case (listed at 64 MiB or more) with its own cloud-only guard: `!cloudOnly && (...)` in SizeProbe.IsDue. No test pins that guard. Case 8's only cloud stand-in, offline.txt, is 1 MiB, so it reaches only the WOF-suspect check, and IsWofSuspect has its own `!cloudOnly`. I deleted `!cloudOnly &&` from IsDue and all 86 tests still passed. The shape that goes through the unpinned branch is the everyday OneDrive placeholder of a large file (EndOfFile of 64 MiB or more, AllocationSize 0, RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS). If the guard regresses, the scanner opens those placeholders, against the design's rule that a cloud-only file is never opened or probed, and no test fails.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/SizeProbe.cs:26-30 (IsDue). tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/OnDiskSizeTests.cs:107-109 (offline.txt is a 1 MiB WOF text file), :128 (Probes == 2). Mutation run: `eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests` with the guard removed gave Passed 86, Failed 0. Restored with `git checkout`, and `git diff --quiet HEAD` confirms the file is clean.
findings.fix: In AFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsAllocatedIsProbedOnlyWhenItIsWof, add a file listed at 64 MiB or more that carries OFFLINE, for example `tree.SparseFile("offline-large.bin", 64 * MiB)` followed by AddAttributes(Offline). Assert it is CloudOnly and not SizeProbed, and keep `Probes == 2`.

findings.claim: The O-008 fix catches `ArgumentException` and all its subclasses as the "rejected path" case. ScanStore.At throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, which derives from ArgumentException, whenever an index is out of range. So an internal indexing bug during a scan is reported as "Could not read <path>" with text like "The store holds N entries. Actual value was M.". The O-008 decision and the as-built doc both say a bug should get the "Scan failed" ending instead. The as-built doc says Scan failed covers "any exception other than the ArgumentException for a relative or empty path", which the code does not do.
findings.fix: Narrow the catch to the root rejection only: `catch (ArgumentException e) when (e.ParamName == "root")`. LongPath.NormalizeRoot throws with nameof(root). Every other ArgumentException then reaches the Scan failed branch.

findings.claim: The design declared four architecture rules, and attempt 2 widened one and added a fifth. The engine's Fitness gate still sees none: there is no .taad/fitness.yaml, so `Fitness op=check` returns NONE, which the gate does not treat as a pass. The rules are enforced only by ArchitectureRulesTests. I read those tests and they pass, and the builder's recorded mutation check shows they fail on a planted violation. But every later slice's gate and review that starts from Fitness will read 'no rules declared'. The builder says it 'cannot edit the engine's declared rule list'. The Fitness tool, however, reads a file in the repo.
findings.evidence: mcp Fitness op=check reports: "NONE. This project declares no architecture rules... Rules go in .taad\fitness.yaml". Fitness op=rules reports: no .taad\fitness.yaml. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs holds the 5 rules as regex tests.
findings.fix: Add .taad/fitness.yaml declaring the five rules (Core does not import System.Windows*/PresentationFramework*/FsAnalyser.App*; the reparse-attribute rule over src/** with its two exceptions; the DirectoryReader-only rule; the never-skipped rule; the interop-only-in-Native rule) with the same patterns ArchitectureRulesTests uses. Keep the tests as well.

obligations.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.cs meets the layout rules: fixed 65,536-entry column pages, 1M-char name pages, page directories allocated up front, and an open-addressing FileIdIndex over the columns. tests/.../ScanStoreTests.cs ScanStoreBudgetTests.FiveMillionEntriesFitTheMemoryBudget checks the 800 MiB store budget at 5M entries and passed in my run.

ScanStore.cs:81-92, with Charges at :210-211: ChargedSize/ChargedOnDisk return 0 for Link and HardlinkDuplicate. tests/.../Scans.cs:12-34 runs AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals after every Scans.Run. CancellationTests.cs:34 and RootTests.cs:45 call it explicitly. HardlinkTests.cs:54-55 and LinkTests.cs:42-43 assert 0 for each duplicate and each link.

LongPathTests.cs:23-63 puts wof. and the a./b. hardlink pair in the trailing-dot folder probe. under a path longer than 400 characters. It asserts SizeProbed on both probed records, HardlinkDuplicate on b., Probes 2 and ProbeFailures 0. ArchitectureRulesTests.InteropLivesOnlyInNative (:65-72) confines (Library|Dll)Import to Native/** plus TestNative.cs. Win32Path and GetNativePath are deferred by the decision.

SizeProbe.cs:23-30 adds LargeFileThreshold (64 MiB) and IsDue. Scanner.cs:165 uses IsDue for newly charged files, and :157-159 skips repeats of a record already settled. OnDiskSizeTests.cs:51-68 is the documentary held-open test, and :74-93 is the growing held-open file charged at 128 MiB with SizeProbed. docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:31-35 says three cases. The large-file branch's cloud guard is untested (see m1).
EntryClassifier.cs:26-27 treats tag 0x8000000A as a Link. Kernel32.cs:31 holds the constant. EntryClassifierTests.cs:20 has the DFS directory row, which passed.

ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:27-36 scans src/**/*.cs and *.xaml, excluding EntryClassifier.cs and Native/Kernel32.cs, for FileAttributes.ReparsePoint, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT, IsReparsePoint and 0x0*400\b. It passes. The engine's Fitness file does not carry the rule (see m3).

ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:50-59 adds \bExplicit\s*=\s*true and Skip(?:Exception) to the three original patterns over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests. The project is on xunit 2.9.3 (FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj), so --fail-skips is deferred as decided.

MainWindow.xaml.cs:146-164: any other exception is caught into failure, and the window shows 'Scan failed: <path>' with the exception type and message. The finally block at :151-160 stops the timer and re-enables the pickers. Subclasses of ArgumentException are still routed to 'Could not read' (see m2).
src/FsAnalyser.Core/CommandLine.cs:11-12 turns a single trailing '"' into '\'. App.xaml.cs:11 calls it. CommandLineTests.cs has 6 rows, all passing.

TempTree.cs:139-152: CreateSymlink catches HResult & 0xFFFF == 1314 and throws an explanation that Developer Mode is off or blocked by policy. There is no fallback and no skip. DirectorySymlink and FileSymlink (:120-134) go through it.

eng/dotnet.ps1:14 sets $SdkVersion = '10.0.401', and :55 passes -Version. Lines :46-52 check that Get-AuthenticodeSignature reports Valid and that the signer matches O=Microsoft Corporation; otherwise the script deletes the installer and exits 1. global.json is unchanged (10.0.100, latestFeature).

docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md covers the open-addressing FileId index, ServerGarbageCollection, the SDDL 0x100080 deny ACE, the flushed sparse fixture, totals excluding the root, CloudOnly on files only, public ScanResult.Root, the m2 ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND note and the m9 text. The engine's stored design record is not updated; that is declared.

MainWindow.xaml.cs:173-192: VolumeInUse returns TotalSize minus TotalFreeSpace for X:\ roots, read on the scan thread. :231 and :260-269 show the gap in Finished and Stopped. docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:89-93 records that explaining the gap is deferred to the coverage-panel slice.

cases.evidence: TraversalTests.ReadsEverythingUnderAFolder builds a\b\c: a's only child is b, and b's only child is c, which holds deep.txt. Beside it: an empty folder, a 0-byte file, and a Hidden|System file plus a Hidden|System folder with a child. It asserts every path, ChildCount 1 for a, ChildCount 0 and FirstChild -1 for the empty folder, that hidden/system entries are counted, and that children are contiguous.

TraversalTests.ListsAFolderThatSpansSeveralBuffers creates 2,000 files with 100-character names. It asserts that the listing needs more than 8 buffers of 64 KiB, and that each name appears exactly once (ordered list equality, so duplicates would fail).

ScanStoreTests.AppendsPastOnePageAndRollsNamesOntoASecondPage appends PageSize+5,000 synthetic entries, with about 2M name characters against a 1M-character name page. It finds the entry that would straddle the name-page boundary and asserts its name, every column, and GetPath across the page boundary.

LongPathTests.ReachesPathsWin32WouldAlter creates, through \\?\, a 255-character component on a path over 400 characters, the names dot., file., 'space ' and NUL, and a WOF file plus a hardlink pair under the deep trailing-dot folder. It asserts Unreadable is empty, the sizes, and SizeProbed with 0 failures. The UNC root is checked as a string mapping.

LinkTests.JunctionsAndSymlinksAreRecordedAndNeverEntered makes junctions and directory symlinks pointing outside the root, inside it, and at the root from inside (a cycle), a dangling directory symlink, and file symlinks pointing outside, inside and at an ancestor. It asserts Kind Link, no children, Charged 0, and nothing under a link.

HardlinkTests.AFileWithSeveralNamesIsChargedOnceAtItsTrueSize has three rows. (2,1): the stale 1 MiB name is seen first, and the first repeat probes and corrects it to 64 MiB. (3,2): three names in three folders, and Probes==1 proves the third name is not probed. (2,0): the reverse order, where the current name is charged and the large-file rule now probes it, as the test comment says.

OnDiskSizeTests.SparseCompressedAndPlainFilesTakeTheListingsOnDiskSize: a 64 MiB sparse file with 4 KiB written and flushed, a 4 MiB LZNT text file, and a 10,000-byte plain file. The sparse file is now probed under the large rule (a declared deviation), and the probe equals the listing. The LZNT and plain files are not probed.

OnDiskSizeTests.AFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsAllocatedIsProbedOnlyWhenItIsWof: a WOF xpress4k file, a 16 MiB all-hole sparse file, a WOF file with OFFLINE, a 200-byte resident file, and a WOF file with a 0x100080 deny ACE. A precondition asserts each is listed with alloc 0 and EOF of at least 4096. It asserts Probes 2 and ProbeFailures 1. The large-file branch's cloud guard is not exercised (m1).

UnreadableFolderTests: b-denied gets a deny FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY ACE and has readable siblings a- and c-. The test asserts a single Unreadable row with error 5, the flag, ChildCount 0, and that both siblings' files are counted.

RootTests covers a regular file (RootError 267), a missing path (2), bare 'C:' (lists the drive root, which contains Windows and not the test dll), relative and empty roots (ArgumentException), and a junction picked as the root (opened through, with 2 files and 300 bytes).

CancellationTests: a ten-folder tree cancelled from AfterFolder when n==3. It asserts listed [1,2,3], the partial totals and the store, and the charged sum. A token cancelled before the call gives Store.Count 0 and AfterFolder is never called.

ListingFallbackTests forces ForceFullDirectoryClass over a real NTFS tree with a hardlink, a junction, a directory symlink and a file symlink. It asserts the same paths, kinds and sizes as a normal scan, FileId 0, no deduplication (Bytes 2050 against 1050), FileIdsAvailable false, and nothing under links.

HardlinkTests.ALoneNameUnderTheRootIsChargedAtItsListingSize: a.bin sits outside the root, b.bin under it is stale after 63 MiB is appended through a.bin. It asserts Flags None, Totals.Bytes 1 MiB and Probes 0, which pins the recorded limit.

drift: docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:41-43 says Scan failed covers every exception except the ArgumentException for a relative or empty path. MainWindow.xaml.cs:142 catches every ArgumentException subclass (filed as m2).

LongPath.NormalizeRoot (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/LongPath.cs:27-34) takes a root that is already in \\?\ or \\?\UNC\ form as-is, without GetFullPath. The design says the root is normalised with GetFullPath, and the as-built doc does not mention the pass-through. It is tested (LongPathTests.NormalisesTheRootOnce rows) and harmless for picker input, but a later reader should know it exists.

The architecture rules exist only as xUnit regex tests (ArchitectureRulesTests.cs) and in the repo doc. The engine's Fitness gate reports that no rules are declared, because .taad/fitness.yaml is absent (filed as m3). The builder declared that it could not edit the design record, but not that the Fitness file was missing.

The engine's stored design for SL-020 still carries the pre-amendment text (two probe cases, HashSet<int>, -Channel 10.0, three endings). docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md supersedes it in the repo. This was declared by the builder.
